summary: Every asset that should cushion stocks is falling with them. Long Treasuries, investment-grade and high-yield credit, gold and crypto all fell over 5 days while the dollar and VIXY rose, and SPY is now only 1.42% above its 200-day with 20-day realized vol at 23.2% going into tonight's Nvidia print. Keep sizing small, keep new risk in Staples, Health Care and Financials, and remember that VOO and VTI share one 200-day stop about 1.4% below the current close.
reasons: Regime is thin: SPY 739.95 vs 200-day 729.58 (+1.42%), down 1.69% over 5 days, 3.05% over 21 and 3.34% over 63. QQQ is already below its 200-day (-2.89%; 21d -6.77%) and IWM is too (-2.01%; 5d -3.39%).

Volatility is rising: SPY 20-day realized vol is 23.2% against 13.8% over 252 days, and VIXY is up 7.41% over 5 days and 10.32% over 21. At that vol a 5-session move inside +/-1% is unlikely, which argues against neutral as much as against risk-on.

Rates are not hedging. TLT fell 3.15% over 5 days (long yields up) and sits 4.01% below its 200-day, and IEF fell 1.70% (2.03% below), so bonds dropped alongside SPY's -1.69%. News memory puts the 10-year at 5.15% with hikes priced for December and January.
Credit is weakening too: HYG -1.01% and LQD -1.79% over 5 days, both below their 200-day (-0.98% and -2.37%).

Signs of a liquidity squeeze: the dollar (UUP) rose 2.04% over 5 days and 5.05% over 63 while gold fell 7.01% over 5 days (13.49% below its 200-day) and BTC fell 18.99% over 21 days. When stores of value are sold alongside equities, the selling is broad de-risking. It is not rotation.
Within equities leadership is defensive. XLP is +1.88% over 5 days, XLU +0.75%, XLE +2.83% and XLF +0.33%, while XLK fell 3.58% over 5 days and 10.2% over 21 days and XLY fell 2.36% over 5.

The counter-evidence, which keeps confidence at 0.5: breadth is better than the cap-weighted index. RSP is 5.34% above its 200-day with 21d +2.26% and fell only 0.91% over 5 days, and SPY is still above its 200-day. My 11-06 risk-off call after a sharp drop was graded wrong (SPY +2.59%). A strong Nvidia print could trigger a short-covering bounce.

asset_class_view.equity_etfs: US core (VOO 1.45% and VTI 1.34% above their 200-day; 21d -3.04% and -2.61%) is still the best of the equity sleeves, but there is little room left above the shared 200-day line, so do not add to it ahead of the Nvidia print. QQQ (below its 200-day, 21d -6.77%) is the riskiest. International is weak with the dollar rising (VXUS 21d -2.92% and 2.74% below its 200-day, VWO 21d -5.46% and 5.69% below). VNQ held up (21d +4.87%, 2.72% above its 200-day), but REITs are exposed to the rise in long yields (TLT -3.15% over 5 days).
asset_class_view.bonds_gold: Neither is working as a hedge right now. TLT is 4.01% below its 200-day, IEF 2.03% below and BND 1.27% below, and long duration fell 3.15% over 5 days alongside equities. SHY (-0.44% over 5 days, 0.42% above its 200-day) is the only near-cash place to hide. Gold is being liquidated: -7.01% over 5 days, -11.45% over 63, 13.49% below its 200-day, vol 29%. Avoid adding gold until it stops falling.
asset_class_view.crypto: Avoid. BTC is -18.99% over 21 days and 11.05% below its 200-day with 44.5% vol. ETH is -21.6% over 21 days and 15.02% below its 200-day with 60.6% vol. News memory shows every downside level being hit within days, driven by ETF outflows and liquidations.

watch: An SPY close below 729.58 (its 200-day, 1.42% below the 739.95 close) turns the regime filter off and trips VOO and VTI together.
The reaction to Nvidia's 11-17 print in QQQ and XLK. A rally that takes QQQ back above its 200-day (now 2.89% below) and SPY up more than 1% would move me to neutral.
TLT and HYG stabilizing (5-day returns turning positive) with UUP rolling over would mean the cross-asset squeeze is easing, and that would weaken this risk-off case.
VIXY's 5-day change turning negative would argue for neutral, and a further rise from +7.41% would strengthen risk-off.
RSP's 21d +2.26% turning negative would show breadth cracking too, which would raise confidence in risk-off.
lessons_applied: None of the active lessons (L2-L9) lists the Market Analyst in applies_to. L8 and L4 note that the PM reads this note's bond and US-core calls. I still say duration is not hedging. My US-core preference stands, but today I add a caution: do not add to VOO or VTI. Per L4 and L8, the 11-16 run read my stance as risk-on. Today's flip to risk-off rests on the cross-asset numbers above. My record is 9 right and 6 wrong (0.60) against an always-neutral baseline of 0.533. The 20-day vol of 23% makes the neutral band less likely than usual, so I picked the side the evidence favors.
